profile.name: Edward Agyapong
bio: I am a master’s student in Economics of Globalisation and European Integration and an Erasmus Mundus Scholarship holder. My research interests lie in applied microeconomics, at the intersection of economic history, international trade, industrial economics, and firm behaviour.

During my master’s, I worked as a Research Assistant with the United Nations University Institute on Comparative Regional Integration Studies and the University of Tartu. I aim to pursue a PhD in Economics and contribute to policy-relevant research and teaching.

Before my master’s, I was a teaching and research assistant at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), contributing to research on poverty and inequality. I taught Advanced Microeconomics to more than 250 undergraduate students, covering game theory, utility theory, firm behaviour, information, insurance, and contract theory.
I hold a first-class honours degree in Economics from KNUST and graduated in the top 1% of a class of 230 students.
